title: Several Circles
spot: Find a circle with a tiny black dot in the middle, like an eye. How many can you count?
story: Kandinsky thought colours worked like music — he even named many paintings "Compositions." Does this one look loud or quiet to you?

title: Discomedusae (Art Forms in Nature, plate 8)
spot: This jellyfish is drawn from below and from the side. Follow one long frilly arm from top to bottom.
story: Haeckel was a scientist who drew the sea creatures he studied, many under a microscope. He named thousands of new species.

title: Composition 8
spot: Find the big black circle, a checkerboard and something that looks like a ladder.
story: Kandinsky painted this while teaching at the Bauhaus, a famous German art and design school. It's one of his calmest, most geometric paintings.

title: Banana Flower and Fruit
place: Metamorphosis of the Insects of Surinam
spot: Find the caterpillar and the moth. Could they be the same animal at different ages?
story: In 1699, at age 52, Merian sailed to South America to study insects and how they change — something almost no woman did back then.

title: Castle and Sun
spot: Count the triangles. Can you find the sun?
story: Klee built this whole castle from simple shapes, like building blocks. He was also a very good violin player.

title: Plum Park in Kameido
place: One Hundred Famous Views of Edo
spot: Which branch is closest to you? Find the people behind the fence.
story: Hiroshige zoomed in on one branch like a photographer. Van Gogh loved this print so much he painted his own copy.

title: Composition II in Red, Blue, and Yellow
spot: Which colour has the biggest box? How many rectangles can you count?
story: Mondrian used only straight lines, black, white, grey and three main colours. He wanted the simplest possible picture to feel perfectly balanced.

title: Forest, British Columbia
spot: Find the path that leads deep into the forest. Where do you think it goes?
story: Carr painted the giant trees of the BC coast so they seem to sway and breathe. She was also a writer and won a Governor General's Award.

title: Suprematist Composition: Airplane Flying
spot: Do these shapes look like an airplane to you? Which way is it flying?
story: Malevich wanted paintings with no objects at all — just pure shapes and colour. He called it Suprematism.

title: Trochilidae (Art Forms in Nature)
spot: How many hummingbirds can you count? Which one has the longest tail?
story: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards. Their hearts can beat more than 1,000 times a minute.

title: The Ten Largest, No. 7, Adulthood
spot: Find spirals, flowers and letters hiding in the swirls.
story: Af Klint painted abstract art years before most famous abstract painters — and asked that it not be shown until 20 years after her death.

title: Silver Sun
spot: Is that a sun, an eye, or something else? What do you see?
story: Dove is often called America's first abstract painter. He tried to paint how nature feels, not just how it looks.

title: Simultaneous Contrasts: Sun and Moon
spot: Where is the sun, and where is the moon?
story: Delaunay was fascinated by how colours seem to change when they sit right next to each other. Try covering half the painting with your hand.

title: North Shore, Lake Superior
spot: What does the tree stump remind you of? Follow the light from the sky.
story: Harris, from Brantford, Ontario, was a founder of the Group of Seven. Later in life his paintings became completely abstract.

title: Senecio
spot: Which eyebrow is raised? What is this face feeling?
story: Klee described drawing as taking a line for a walk. This whole face is built from a circle, squares and triangles.

title: Ascending Forms
spot: Find the black circles stacked like a tower. What's at the very top?
story: In 1927 Brooker showed abstract paintings at the Arts and Letters Club in Toronto — the first abstract art exhibition by a Canadian artist.

title: Yellow-Red-Blue
spot: Find a yellow shape, a red one and a blue one. Which one feels the loudest?
story: Kandinsky believed yellow felt warm and bright, and blue felt calm and deep. Do you agree?

title: Brooklyn Bridge
spot: Find the bridge cables, the arches and the city lights.
story: Stella came to New York from Italy and saw the Brooklyn Bridge as a great cathedral made of steel.
